mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up our journey through Braiding Sweetgrass, I hope you’re noticing the world with fresh eyes. The heart of these stories isn’t just about plants or science or tradition—it’s about building relationships. It’s all about learning to see life as a gift, tuning in to what the land is quietly teaching us, and finding where you truly belong in this beautiful web we all share. So, what really matters here? Gratitude—it’s something you can practice every day, deepening your connection to the world around you. Remember, plants and land aren’t just resources; they’re relatives and teachers, worthy of our respect. When you blend science with Indigenous wisdom, you get a much richer, more caring way of understanding. Ceremony and story help us remember our place, and what we owe to each other. And living with limits—being mindful about what you take and what you give back—makes sure there’s enough for everyone, now and for the future. To bring this all together, just know that every small act of care truly counts. You don’t have to be an expert or stand on a stage to make a difference. Start simple: notice the gifts that surround you, offer thanks to the land, and share what you can. Listen to the stories that others carry, and share your own. Get curious—learn the names of the plants and animals that share your home. Try practicing the Honorable Harvest: take only what you need, and always give something back. The world is out there, waiting for your attention, your care, and your hope. Real healing—for the land and for ourselves—happens when we choose to live in relationship, with humility, patience, and love. The braid isn’t ever finished. Every day, you have a chance to add a new strand—to help weave a future where people and the earth can thrive together. So let your actions, no matter how small, become part of that ongoing story.
